title: Optimization of cassava grafting technique to enhance its adoption in cultivation
author: Opoku-Agyemang, Amissah, et al.
materials:
1.
Sterilization of grafting tools and equipment

steps.title: Sterilize tools and hands
steps.instruction: Sterilize razor blades and grafting clips with 70 % ethanol followed by 10 % bleach, and sanitize hands with 70 % ethanol before any grafting work.

steps.title: Select and prepare seedlings
steps.instruction: Choose 5‑week‑old cassava seedlings that have a stem diameter of ~6–10 mm, stem height of 20–30 cm, and at least 10 leaves; irrigate the seedlings adequately before grafting.

steps.title: Prepare rootstock and scion
steps.instruction: Create a 1.0 cm vertical slit (cleft) in the rootstock; cut the scion tip into a wedge shape so that the cambial surfaces match the slit.

steps.title: Perform grafting
steps.instruction: Insert the wedge‑shaped scion into the vertical slit of the rootstock, align the cambial regions as closely as possible, and secure the graft joint with a grafting clip.

steps.title: Prune leaves
steps.instruction: Remove all leaves from the rootstock and retain only two small young leaves on the apical portion of the scion to reduce transpiration.

steps.title: Set up wooden healing chamber
steps.instruction: Place the grafted seedlings into a homemade wooden healing chamber; mist the interior with 150 mL of clean water, then cover the chamber first with a white plastic sheet (to reflect light) and subsequently with a black plastic sheet (to absorb light and maintain 25–35 °C).

steps.title: Maintain healing conditions
steps.instruction: Keep chamber humidity between 80–95 % (overall optimum 70–98 %) and temperature 25–35 °C. Keep the chamber completely closed for the first 2–3 days, then open it and mist frequently for a further 12–13 days while inspecting plants, removing any adventitious roots with scissors. Avoid misting directly on the graft junction; instead, place pots in clean water for 2–5 min to allow water uptake.

steps.title: Acclimatize in greenhouse
steps.instruction: After 15 days post‑grafting, move seedlings to a greenhouse; gradually introduce light and lower humidity over the next 30 days, watering carefully to avoid damage to the graft union.

steps.title: Remove grafting clips
steps.instruction: Detach the grafting clips once the union is strong, typically 30–40 days after grafting.

steps.title: Transplant to field
steps.instruction: Transplant grafted plants 50–60 days after grafting using a planting distance of 1.0 m between rows and 0.9 m within rows, and apply all recommended crop‑management practices.

description: Grafting, the act of explanting a scion onto a rootstock has been a useful technique in the fields of agricultural and plant science. While grafting has been widely adopted in various horticultural crops, its application in cassava has been limited, notably, in Africa. In response to this gap, we present the first report of an optimized cleft grafting protocol for cassava developed in Africa. The development of an optimized cassava grafting protocol with illustrative elements including stepwise photos and videos that allows reliable grafting is essential to obtaining reproducible results with high success rates. To observe the optimum growth and vigor status of the cassava seedlings for grafting, the vegetative growth of the cassava seedlings at 42 DAP was measured. The cassava seedlings (Fig. 4a–b) exhibited growth in stem diameter (6 mm – 9 mm), plant height (30 cm – 50 cm), number of leaves (12 – 19) and chlorophyll content (26.6 µmol cm-2 – 48.4 µmol cm-2) (Fig. 4c–f).
